newsitem.title: USA: CFTC to decide CBOT delivery issue as soon as July.
newsitem.headline: CFTC to decide CBOT delivery issue as soon as July.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission could act as soon as late July on controversial delivery changes proposed for corn and soybean contracts, the CFTC head told Reuters Thursday.
"I would hope we would act within the near future, meaning within the next month or two," said Brooksley Born, head of the agency.

CFTC is reviewing and analyzing more than 650 public comments -- mostly opposed to the Chicago Board of Trade's proposed changes -- before issuing a decision, she said. If the agency decides the exchange's proposal would not protect market integrity, the CFTC could order its own version of delivery terms.
"Our economic analysis division is making sure that it has all the data necessary to analyze the situation, and is well along in the process of its analysis," Born said.

CBOT's proposal to drop the port of Toledo and replace it with a series of delivery points along the northern Illinois River set off a storm of criticism, mostly from farm groups, elevators and state and federal lawmakers in Ohio.
Last week, CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said the exchange would go to court if the agency rejected the plan.
CFTC prodded the exchange into proposing a change in delivery terms after becoming concerned about dwindling grain warehouse availability in the Chicago area.

"This is a problem that the CBOT has had with its delivery points for more than a decade, as the CBOT is well aware," Born said. "We are required by law to administer the Commodity Exchange Act and that's what we're doing."

Several concerned lawmakers in Washington have asked the Justice Department's antitrust division to examine the potential concentration of ownership among barge companies and warehouses under the CBOT proposal. And another lawmaker has asked the General Accounting Office to investigate the issue as well.
"I'm not sure whether the antitrust division or the GAO is going to want to have input into the process," Born said.
CBOT submitted its proposed changes to the agency in April.
Born also said the agency was closely watching the CBOT to see how it responded to the agency's similar delivery concerns over the exchange's wheat contract.
"I am hopeful that the CFTC will take action to explore the delivery options" for its wheat contract, she added.
